Bug_Details:
Invalid time zone identifier. TimeZone.getTimeZone(String) will silently return GMT instead of the time zone you intended. TimeZone.getTimeZone(String) silently returns GMT when an invalid time zone
identifier is passed in.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is demonstrated by passing an invalid time zone ID to TimeZone.getTimeZone(String). If the ID is invalid, the method returns a TimeZone object for GMT, rather than throwing an error or returning null, which can silently cause logic errors in the program.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case triggers the bug by passing an invalid time zone ID to the showBug method. The method TimeZone.getTimeZone(String) will silently return GMT if the ID is invalid. We assert that the result should not be "GMT", expecting it to be something else, but due to the bug, it returns "GMT", causing the test to fail.
